2609.01404.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs as Generalist Vision-Language-Action Agents for Drone Control: Commanding, Approaching, Tracking and Searching
2609.01404.paper_summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are strong perceivers of images and video. We ask how far that reach extends into acting: dropping an MLLM directly into a drone's control loop, with its entire action space declared solely in the prompt. Recent systems approach this setting but increasingly narrow the model's decision-making. We widen it back. We introduce DroneCATS-Agent, an architecture where the MLLM is a swappable component, and DroneCATS, a benchmark treating the model as the independent variable. Beyond merely flying toward a pixel, our agent entrusts the model to yaw and search, deliberate when unsure, and self-declare arrival---all without fine-tuning or function-calling schemas. Evaluating frontier and open models across four core capabilities---approaching a visible target, tracking a moving one, searching outside the initial view, and commanding a multi-drone fleet---reveals that even the simplest embodied settings are far from solved. Crucially, to identify what breaks first at the edge, our roster scales down to 2B parameters. The findings expose a stark paradox: it is not the flying that fails. Small open models often navigate into the success radius more reliably than frontier models, yet lose the episode by declaring arrival prematurely or not at all. Multi-drone commanding amplifies this divide, with small models failing by blindly copying a single coordinate across distinct views. Viewed as vision-language-action agents, the models' spatial perception holds up, but their action protocol does not. What separates a deployable edge model from a frontier model is not navigation, but the discipline to sustain a declared protocol and emit the correct terminating action. The open problem is closing this gap at onboard compute costs---yielding a fast model that plans persistently and knows exactly when it is done---and DroneCATS is built to measure that distance.
2609.01404.paper_summary_zh: 多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）是強大的圖像和視頻感知者。我們詢問這種能力在行動中的延伸範圍：將一個MLLM直接放入無人機的控制迴路中，並在提示中僅聲明其整個行動空間。最近的系統接近這一設置，但越來越多地縮小模型的決策範圍。我們將其擴大回來。我們介紹了DroneCATS-Agent，一種架構，其中MLLM是一個可替換的組件，而DroneCATS是一個將模型視為自變量的基準測試。除了僅僅飛向一個像素之外，我們的代理信任模型進行偏航和搜索，在不確定時進行深思熟慮，並自我聲明到達——所有這些都不需要微調或函數調用方案。對四個核心能力進行前沿和開放模型的評估——接近可見目標、跟踪移動目標、在初始視野之外搜索，以及指揮多無人機艦隊——揭示即使是最簡單的具身設置也遠未解決。關鍵是，為了確定邊緣處首先破裂的原因，我們的名單縮小到2B參數。這些發現揭示了一個明顯的悖論：失敗的不是飛行。小型開放模型往往比前沿模型更可靠地導航進入成功半徑，但卻因為過早或根本不聲明到達而失去該回合。多無人機指揮擴大了這一差距，小型模型因盲目複製不同視圖中的單個坐標而失敗。作為視覺-語言-行動代理，這些模型的空間感知能力保持良好，但其行動協議卻不然。使可部署的邊緣模型與前沿模型區分開來的不是導航，而是維持聲明協議並發出正確終止行動的紀律。當前的開放問題是以板載計算成本縮小這一差距——產生一個持續計劃並確切知道何時完成的快速模型——而DroneCATS旨在測量這一距離。
